findings.claim: Making the lab required on Standard adds about 30 minutes of required work (lab.json minutes setup 8 + tasks 22) that no catalog or evidence text places on the Standard calendar. The module covers S1-S2, which the course intake (authoring/evidence/spring-boot/intake.md, day table rows S1 and S2) records as Concept days with requiredLab false and no lab overlay, Two intake sentences now contradict the change. Line 659 says S9 and S12 'are the two required Standard coding labs', and the 'No lab, with reason' paragraph (line 663) still says spring-boot-basics has no lab. The changed catalog notes (module.json sourceCoverageNotes line 27; the five topic.json lab.reason strings) now say 'required Standard practice' but also 'outside the calendar lab overlay', and nothing in the repository names the Standard day or block that holds the work. Every other required Spring lab (validation-errors-and-testing S9, api-security S12) sits on a calendar requiredLab day, and their module.json notes say so. A repository precedent for a required Standard lab on a Concept day (html-css-js/dom-tooling-and-async, trackRequirement standard required, S25) names its slot in README line 3: the 40-minute Faded then fresh block. S2 page budgets already total 58 minutes and the S2 mastery check (blueprint dayId S2) adds up to 15, so placement matters for honest timing within the 120-minute day.
findings.recommendation: Record where the required 30 minutes runs on Standard, for example a practice block of the frozen S2 Concept-day template (html-css-js uses the 40-minute Faded then fresh block for this), after the four S2 pages and before or after the S2 mastery check (whose instructions already sequence the check 'before the module coding lab'), and state that placement in module.json's coding-lab note. Flag the two stale intake sentences (lines 659 and 663) for a course-level follow-up branch, since this module branch may not edit course evidence.

findings.claim: The learner-facing README does not contradict the new status, but it is silent on it: nothing tells a Standard learner that this lab is now required or tells a Fast learner they may skip it, and it gives no day or time estimate. The two sibling required Spring labs open with 'This is the required lab of the Standard track's ... day' (validation-errors-and-testing and api-security README line 5), and html-css-js/dom-tooling-and-async names its track, day and block in README line 3. A learner moving across the Spring labs therefore cannot tell from the bundle that this one changed from optional to required.
findings.recommendation: Add one Goal sentence matching the sibling labs, naming the Standard day or block from spring-basics-req-edu-001, that the lab is required on Standard and not required on Fast, and roughly 30 minutes (8 setup, 22 tasks). This changes README bytes, so it re-stales lab-run.json and the SME critic binding; batch it with the evidence refresh this change already needs.

findings.claim: Two more objective claims cover less than the objective text, the same kind of gap as spring-practice-edu-008. That matters more now that the lab is required evidence of those objectives. (1) Line 15 claims path-query-and-body-parameters#o1 ('Bind a path variable, a required and an optional query parameter and a JSON request body'). The lab practices the path variable (Task 2), the optional query parameter (Task 4) and the body (Task 5), but no task binds a required query parameter. (2) Line 13 claims dependency-injection-replacing-manual-wiring#o1 ('Replace the manual new-based wiring of a controller, service and repository with Spring-managed components that receive their dependencies through constructors'). Task 1 replaces one manual new in the controller with constructor injection of a @Bean-provided catalog; there is no service or repository layer and no component-scanned class to wire. The core move is practiced; the three-layer scope is not.
findings.recommendation: Do not grow the lab (the 22-minute task budget is reasonable as it stands). Record the partial coverage next to the edu-008 note in the module catalog: the required query parameter is covered by the mastery check's prediction items (path-query#o2) and the page, and the layered wiring is taught by the S3 page constructor-injection-across-layers and applied in part by the porting-and-configuration lab (S3), where the learner injects a shipped service into the controller. Or narrow the claims if the catalog convention lets a lab claim part of an objective.
